portal-01-topics.png.t: Project picker — shows the project you are in. ServiceHub needs its Project ID, which is the part after projects/ in a topic's full name below (not the project's display name).
Topic IDs — where messages are published. ServiceHub finds every topic in the project; you do not list them.
Topic name — the full path. The part after projects/ is your Project ID, the first thing you type into ServiceHub.

portal-02-subscriptions.png.t: Subscription IDs — a queue in ServiceHub is a subscription together with its topic. The one ending -dlq-subscription holds your dead letters.
Topic — the topic each subscription reads from.
Ack deadline — how long a reader has to acknowledge a message before Pub/Sub delivers it again. ServiceHub hands a looked-at message straight back, so it never waits this out.

portal-03-subscription-dead-letter.png.t: Dead lettering — the tab for the same policy, where you can change it.
Dead letter topic — where Pub/Sub forwards a message after it fails too often. ServiceHub reads this topic’s own subscription as your dead letters.

Maximum delivery attempts — after this many failed tries Pub/Sub forwards the message. Reading a dead letter from ServiceHub counts as one more attempt, which is why ServiceHub only looks when you ask.

portal-04-service-accounts.png.t: Create service account — start here to make an account just for ServiceHub, not your own.
The ServiceHub account — separate from your own and from the accounts your applications use, so you can switch it off later without disturbing anything else.
Status — Enabled. Disabling or deleting the account cuts ServiceHub off.

portal-05-iam-roles.png.t: Grant access — where you give an account a role on the whole project.

The ServiceHub account with Pub/Sub Viewer on the project — it lets ServiceHub list your topics and subscriptions. Pub/Sub Subscriber and Pub/Sub Publisher are granted on the individual subscriptions and topics (next screenshot).

portal-06-topic-permissions.png.t: Add principal — grants a role on just this topic. Do the same on each subscription for Pub/Sub Subscriber.
Pub/Sub Publisher — granted to the ServiceHub account on this topic only. It is used to put a replayed message back.
Pub/Sub Viewer — inherited from the project, so the account can see this topic.

portal-07-keys.png.t: Google’s reminder that keys are a risk if they leak. Treat the file like a password, and delete the key when you no longer need it.
Add key → Create new key → JSON — downloads the key file ServiceHub needs. Google shows the private key only once.
The key — Active. The bin deletes it, which is how you revoke ServiceHub’s access later.
